forces.title: Accelerating AI Adoption Drives Digital Infrastructure Demand
forces.description: Accelerating adoption of AI technologies across various industries is creating sustained demand for underlying digital infrastructure. This includes robust network connectivity and passive infrastructure to support the increased data processing and transmission requirements of AI workloads. Public and private investment in digital infrastructure is underpinned by this trend, contributing to the long-term strength and growth prospects of the sector.

forces.title: Digital Infrastructure Universe Expansion Beyond Traditional Assets
forces.description: The digital infrastructure category is undergoing a dramatic expansion, moving beyond traditional communications assets like cell towers to include data centers, edge facilities, power-linked assets, and AI-specific retrofits. This broadens the scope of potential revenue streams and partnerships for tower and passive infrastructure companies, requiring operators to adapt their portfolios and strategic frameworks to capture value from this evolving ecosystem.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Cell Towers Maintain Predictable Revenue and Infrastructure-Style Underwriting
forces.description: Amidst the expanding and diversifying digital infrastructure landscape, cell towers continue to exhibit highly attractive economic criteria. They are characterized by near-zero churn and strong cash-flow visibility, supported by predictable, long-term contracts. This "infrastructure-style underwriting" contrasts with more volatile, execution-heavy digital assets, providing stability and continued investor confidence in their annuity-like rental revenue model as passive infrastructure.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: AI-Driven Valuations for Infrastructure-Layer Assets
forces.description: The M&A market is seeing a clear bifurcation, with infrastructure-layer assets, including components crucial for AI such as data centers, computing, and power infrastructure, commanding extraordinary valuations. This is driven by visible, contractually backed demand from AI workloads. This trend positions existing and developing tower and passive infrastructure as highly attractive to investors seeking exposure to the fundamental enablers of AI, suggesting significant capital appreciation potential.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: Digital Infrastructure as Strategic National Security Investment Theme
forces.description: Digital infrastructure, including passive components, has emerged as a distinct investment theme with significant backing from national security spending, industrial policy, and sovereignty concerns. Governments prioritize domestic AI infrastructure development, as exemplified by SoftBank's €75 billion pledge in France for an AI network. This governmental and strategic focus creates a durable demand backdrop and unique valuation drivers for these assets, supporting long-term investment.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: Rising Energy Costs and Supply Chain Constraints for Digital Infrastructure
forces.description: The broader digital infrastructure sector faces near-term uncertainty due to several factors impacting operating costs and project timelines. Higher energy costs for data centers, semiconductor supply constraints, and rising cyber risks are significant concerns. For passive infrastructure, this could translate into increased operational expenses (e.g., for power at tower sites) and potential delays or cost overruns in new builds or upgrades, necessitating careful management of these exposures.

forces.title: Permitting and Grid Connection Delays for New Infrastructure Capacity
forces.description: The rapid build-out of digital infrastructure, particularly data centers, is significantly hampered by speed-of-execution challenges. Labor shortages, equipment lead times, permitting delays, and slow grid connections prevent new capacity from coming online quickly enough. Up to 50% of global data center capacity expected in 2026 could be delayed. While more directly impacting data centers, this creates bottlenecks for the entire digital ecosystem, including passive infrastructure components requiring power and local approvals.
forces.source_title: Colocation data centers: The infrastructure race behind AI

forces.title: Shifting Investor Focus from Broad Asset Classes to Asset-Specific Performance
forces.description: Investors are increasingly moving away from broad asset class distinctions in digital infrastructure, focusing instead on asset-level performance. Key indicators like churn rates, renewal behavior, repricing frequency, and capital intensity are crucial for determining whether an asset is a long-duration yield investment or an execution-heavy growth business. This shift requires tower and passive infrastructure operators to clearly articulate and demonstrate the stable, long-term value inherent in their specific assets.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: AI Investment Provides Economic Cushion and Productivity Gains
forces.description: On a macro level, significant AI investment is acting as a strong economic cushion, helping to navigate global disruptions. For the UK, AI is projected to boost labor productivity by 3.4% and contribute 1.7% to GDP over the next decade. This positive macroeconomic backdrop, driven by technological advancement, indirectly benefits digital infrastructure providers, including those in towers and passive infrastructure, by fostering an environment of sustained technological investment and economic growth.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

viewpoints.title: Digital Infrastructure Bolsters Telecom Sector Amidst Geopolitical Headwinds
viewpoints.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector demonstrates resilience, supported by consistent public and private investment in digital infrastructure. This sustained investment, coupled with accelerating AI adoption, provides a strong foundation for long-term growth. However, higher data-centre energy costs, semiconductor supply constraints, and increasing cyber risks introduce near-term uncertainties. Businesses are advised to manage these external pressures carefully while capitalizing on opportunities in AI and enhanced connectivity, maintaining overall strong fundamentals with prudent credit assessment.

viewpoints.title: Cell Towers Maintain Strong Infrastructure-Style Underwriting Amidst Market Changes
viewpoints.description: The digital infrastructure universe is rapidly expanding, driven by AI and evolving technology. While some digital assets, like B2C fiber, face increased operational complexity and valuation challenges, cell towers continue to demonstrate strong, long-duration, infrastructure-style underwriting characteristics. This resilience stems from near-zero churn and high cash-flow visibility through predictable, long-term contracts, making them distinct from other execution-heavy assets. This suggests a continued stable and attractive investment profile for passive tower infrastructure.
viewpoints.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

viewpoints.title: Digital Infrastructure Commands Extraordinary Valuations Driven by AI Demand
viewpoints.description: The M&A market in mid-2026 is significantly influenced by AI, leading to a bifurcation in valuations across the technology sector. Infrastructure-layer assets, including data centers, computing, and power (and by extension, related digital infrastructure like towers), are attracting extraordinary valuations. This is attributed to visible demand secured by contracts, highlighting a strong investor appetite for fundamental infrastructure supporting AI. This indicates a very positive outlook for foundational digital infrastructure assets like towers, positioning them as a high-conviction investment theme.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain
